item.title: Shutdown deal struck after failed Senate vote
item.description: Senate Democrats and the White House reached an agreement late Thursday to fund most departments and agencies through Sept. 30 after a previous funding bill was blocked.

item.title: Law enforcement is the leading DHS use case for AI
item.description: Subagencies like ICE and CBP are leveraging biometric technologies like facial recognition extensively, per the new case inventory.

item.title: VA secretary: EHR deployments are ‘going to be done in the right way’
item.description: VA Secretary Doug Collins told lawmakers they “have every right to be skeptical” as EHR go-lives resume in April but said the modernization project is back on track.

item.title: NIST releases a new draft cybersecurity framework for systems that never stop moving
item.description: Sometimes the most important cybersecurity work is not flashy.

item.title: As Trump administration cries ‘fraud,’ experts worry it does more harm than good
item.description: “It’s dismaying,” one longtime anti-fraud expert told Nextgov/FCW of how the administration is using fraud as rationale but firing the watchdogs that are tasked with finding it.

item.title: GSA quietly rolls out CMMC-like cybersecurity framework for contractors
item.description: The General Services Administration's new requirements for protecting controlled unclassified information apply immediately to new contracts, at the contracting officer's discretion.

item.title: Federal CIO says he’s zeroed in on government service delivery
item.description: That effort has new accountability levers and top-down support that can be helpful in driving change, CX leaders from the Office of Management and Budget said Friday.

item.title: Tech Bills of the Week: Measures seek to boost cyber posture of utilities
item.description: The proposed legislation would expand the Energy Department’s role in hardening U.S. energy infrastructure to boost cybersecurity and physical protections for pipelines, electric utilities and local distribution systems.

item.title: Agencies are prioritizing flexibility and cost savings in AI purchases, GSA official says
item.description: GSA’s acting Assistant Commissioner Lawrence Hale from the General Services Administration said early demand has been focused on AI tools that support everyday work and productivity.

item.title: Key cyber statutes at risk again as Congress works to avert shutdown
item.description: One measure allows the private sector to provide threat data to government agencies with key legal protections in place.
